title: What if Earth tipped over on its side? 🌍
subject: earth
description:
Could your city handle 80 days without a sunset? 👇

Earth leans 23.5 degrees, which gives us mild seasons. Uranus leans almost 98. Here's what a sideways Earth would do to day, night and the poles.

Sources: NASA Science, "Uranus: Facts" (tilt 97.77°, 21-year polar winter); Phys.org/Astrobiology Magazine, "High planetary tilt lowers odds for life?" (Feb 2012, quoting René Heller, Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam); day-length figures calculated from orbital geometry for New York's latitude (40.7°N).

scenes.text: Tip Earth sideways, and your summer Sun never sets.
Today the planet leans 23.5 degrees. Uranus leans almost 98, and each half of it sits through a 21-year winter.
At 90 degrees, New York would get about 80 days of daylight with no night at all.
Six months later, about 80 days of total darkness.
scenes.nasa: city lights at night from ISS

scenes.text: René Heller, a Potsdam astrophysicist, put it plainly: one pole boils while the other freezes in the dark.
Only the equator would keep 12-hour days all year.
